verses.1: And it happened that he spoke to Shaul. Jehovah Nathan’s spirit was connected to David’s spirit. And Jehovah Nathan loved him as if he were his own son.
verses.2: And Shaul took him that day. They did not allow him to return to his father’s house.
verses.3: And Jonathan and David made a covenant with each other, loving each other completely.
verses.4: And Jonathan stripped off the armor that was on him, and he gave it to David and his men. It was given to them until the end of time.
verses.5: David went out with all those whom Saul sent him. Saul assigned them to the soldiers who were involved in warfare. This pleased everyone in the people, as well as the servants of Saul.
verses.6: And when David returned from his journey, after he had defeated the Philistines, the women of Israel went out from all the cities of Israel to sing and praise the Lord, the king, with joy and celebration.
verses.7: And the women who were playing games said, “Shaul struck them with his spear, and David with his arrows.”
verses.8: And Shaul was very angry. This situation displeased him greatly. He said, “They gave David many treasures, but to me they gave only hundreds. But the queen is still theirs.”
verses.9: And Shaul became a rival to David from that day onward.
verses.10: And in the evening, a spirit of God came upon Shaul. He was brought inside the house. David played music with his hand that day. And the harp was in Shaul’s hands.
verses.11: And Shaul took the chariot, and said, “Akhéh David!” And David was moved away from his side.
verses.12: And Shaul saw that David was with God. And from Shaul’s side, there was peace.
verses.13: Shaul took him away from his people. He put him in charge of a thousand men. Then he went out and stood before the people.
verses.14: And David was wise in all his ways. And Jehovah was with him.
verses.15: And Shaul saw that he was extremely intelligent, and he was afraid of him.
verses.16: And all of Israel and Judah love David, because he comes before them.
verses.17: Shaul said to David, “Look, my eldest daughter is very beautiful. I will give her to you as a wife. But she must be the bride of my son. She must also fight in battles for Jehovah.” Shaul added, “Let my hand not be involved in this matter; let it be the hands of Philistines who will do this work.”
verses.18: And David said to Shaul, “Who am I, and who are my ancestors from the tribe of my father in Israel, that I should be a bridegroom for the king?”
verses.19: And it happened that when Tamar, the daughter of Shaul, was given to David, she was given as a wife to Adriel, the prophet.
verses.20: And Michal, the daughter of Saul, fell in love with David. They told this to Saul, and he took this matter into consideration.
verses.21: And Shaul said to her, “Let it be a burden for you. Let it become a source of trouble for you. It will also become a tool in the hands of the Philistines.” Then Shaul said to David, “In two days, you will share this with me.”
verses.22: And Shaul commanded his servants to speak to David, saying, “Look, the king desires you, and all his servants love you. Now, come and be with the king.”
verses.23: And the servants of Shaul spoke these words to David. David said, “In your eyes, he has become king. But I am a simple man; I will not become king.”
verses.24: And the servants of Shaul told him, “These are the words spoken by David.”
verses.25: And Shaul said, “As David said, there is no need for a king to die quickly. There are hundreds of Philistines who can take revenge on the king’s enemies. Shaul wanted to overthrow David through the hands of the Philistines.”
verses.26: And his servants told David these things. David listened to them carefully, in order to become king. But those days still hadn’t come yet.
verses.27: David stood up and went along with his men. They traveled through Philistia. David brought along his wives, and they became queenly in the king’s court. Shaul gave him his daughter in marriage.
verses.28: Shaul saw that Jehovah was with David and with the daughter of Shaul’s wife. He knew that Jehovah loved them both.
verses.29: And Shaul continued to oppose David from behind. Shaul always hated David throughout all those days.
verses.30: And the servants of Phileas went out. As soon as they left, David became smarter than all the servants of Saul. His name became very famous.
